"Sea-salt morning. Lucky kid — you got the last starter."
"Professor said you might come by. Don't keep her waiting."
"Grab a relic before you head out. The first route is rougher than it reads."
"Whole town fits on a postcard. Folks here measure trainers by who left and who came back."
"Old place by the water's got its lights on again. Nobody's seen who lives there in years."
"Mind the tall grass past the gate. Small things in there with big opinions."
"Quarry shift just ended — the gym's where they drink off the dust."
"Gym Leader likes to test endurance. Heal first, swagger later."
"Mart's open all night. Potions don't carry to the next run, so use them."
"The dust gets in everything — your boots, your lungs, your win record."
"Dojo's free to watch, costly to enter. Same as most things worth doing."
"House at the quarry's edge stays unlocked. Nobody locks it; nobody goes in."
"Every barista in this town can recite a movepool. It's embarrassing."
"The Move Tutor knows tricks the schools won't teach. Bring gold."
"Dojo Master once boxed a Machamp. Allegedly. Still — don't test him."
"Bring a notebook. The Tutor talks fast, and a second hearing costs extra."
"The cafés argue type charts till closing. Don't take a side near the gym crowd."
"Kid down the lane keeps a list of every trainer who passes through. Swears she's seen your name before. She's wrong, probably."
"The students hold mock leagues in the quad. Don't lose to a freshman — they'll publish."
"Nature Rater keeps office hours. Make an appointment, like everyone else."
"Half the textbooks here will be wrong by next year. The Gym Leader won't."
"Lecture halls run late. So do the rematches in the quad."
"There's a shelf in the library nobody reshelves. Take what you find; leave what finds you."
"Freshmen publish your losses, seniors publish your wins. Pick your enemies early."
"Ranger boots, hunter boots, poacher boots — every kind of mud meets at this gate."
"Safari Zone takes your money and your patience. Sometimes it gives back."
"Don't catch what you can't train. The Underground will buy what you can't keep."
"Past the gate it's mud and patience. The Zone doesn't bargain."
"Rangers count everyone in. They count everyone out, too. Usually the numbers match."
"Don't name what you might have to release. It costs more that way."
"Half the badges in this town were earned at the slots. Don't ask which half."
"Casino payouts are real. Casino odds are realer."
"You can hear the Gym Leader from the rooftop bar. She likes a crowd."
"Last easy night before the climb. Spend it or don't — the slots don't care either way."
"Fountain shuts off at midnight. Some nights it keeps running anyway. Maintenance, they say."
"Win big and the floor remembers your face. Lose big and so does the alley."
"This city eats trainers and prints champions. Take notes."
"Department Store sells what you need. The alley sells what you don't."
"Colress is on the top floor. He hates waiting. Move fast."
"Twelve floors of want, one roof lab, and an alley for everything in between."
"Colress studies you whether you asked or not. Mind which questions you answer."
"Big screen in the square loops the same champion's walk-on. Same face for as long as anyone bothers to remember."
"Thin air at the pass keeps the tourists down in the lowlands. Mostly."
"Veterans drink here between rematches. Buy a round, hear a story."
"League gates open at dawn. They close on the unworthy."
"Thin air, thinner patience. The League's close enough to taste up here."
"Every story at this altitude is a warning wearing a smile."
"Somebody walks the pass at night who shouldn't be able to. Wears a cap like yours. The veterans stopped pointing it out."
"Last gym before the Plateau. Pilgrims travel weeks to lose here."
"The bells ring for every challenger. They don't ring twice."
"A masked figure was asking after you. Wouldn't give a name."
"Bells, pilgrims, and one last gate. Past it the cities run out."
"The masked one came through again. Asked the bell-keeper how you were doing — by name."
"Take the long look back. Six routes made you; the seventh won't be a route."
"This is the room. No badges past that door — only legacies."
"Cameras are rolling. Smile or don't. It's your face."
"Welcome to the Plateau, trainer. Try not to flinch."
"Past this door it's legacies, not badges. Different currency entirely."
"The portrait wall has one empty frame at the end. Clean glass. Nobody ever books it."
"Cameras love a flincher. Don't give them the shot."
"This is it. The road goes one way from here, and not back."
"Nerves are the body's way of admitting you care."
"The gate opens for the worthy. The rest learn to read."
"One way in. This road forgot how to go back a long time ago."
"Bring everything. The road keeps whatever you can't carry."
"People hear a second set of footsteps in here. Always one behind. Always keeping pace."
"Trainers still gather here, even after the credits roll."
"Hall of Fame is just over there. Your name should still be on it."
"The Underground broker has been asking about you. Quietly."
"Credits rolled and nobody left. Tells you something about the worthy."
"The broker's questions got sharper since you took the wall. He smiles more, too."
"Your name's on the Hall. Go look. Some mornings folks swear the date beside it reads wrong."
